common_name: Purple Prince Zinnia (Heirloom Rich Wine-Purple Dahlia-Flowered Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Purple Prince is a long-cultivated heirloom zinnia, grown since at least 1949, bearing fully to semi-double, rich wine-purple dahlia-form blooms.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 12-18 inches. Purple Prince, an heirloom zinnia grown since at least 1949 and holder of a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit, bears large, fully to semi-double, rich wine-purple dahlia-form blooms on tall, sturdy stems well suited to cutting. Plants bloom heavily from midsummer through the first frost with regular deadheading or harvesting to encourage continuous production. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.

common_name: Uproar Scarlet Zinnia (Huge Uniform Scarlet-Red Disease-Tolerant Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Uproar Scarlet bears huge, uniform scarlet-red flower heads on sturdy, disease-tolerant plants, a modern cut-flower breeding introduction.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 12-18 inches. Uproar Scarlet bears exceptionally large, uniform, brilliant scarlet-red blooms on tall, sturdy, disease-tolerant plants bred specifically for reliable cut-flower production, standing out for its consistency of flower size and vivid, saturated color across the entire planting. Plants bloom heavily from midsummer through the first frost with regular deadheading or harvesting to encourage continuous production. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.
sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 12-18 inches. Aurora bears large, two-tone blooms in soft, vintage-inspired color combinations with a contrasting center, a subtler, more nuanced palette than solid-colored zinnia cultivars, popular among floral designers seeking muted, antique-toned bouquets. sources: Association of Specialty Cut Flower Growers

Linen bears large, fully double blooms in soft cream and blush tones, an understated, neutral color that pairs well with almost any bouquet or garden color scheme and has made it a favorite among cut-flower growers seeking a versatile neutral. common_name: Crystal White Zinnia (AAS-Winning Pure White Single Daisy-Form Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Crystal White, a 1997 All-America Selections winner, bears pure white, single daisy-like blooms.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 8-12 inches. Crystal White, a 1997 All-America Selections winner, bears crisp, pure white, single daisy-form flowers with a yellow-green center disk on a compact, uniform, heavily branched plant, offering a clean, simple bloom form distinct from the fully double dahlia-type zinnias. Its compact size suits edging, containers, and mass bedding as well as cutting. Plants bloom heavily from midsummer through the first frost with regular deadheading. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.

common_name: Zahara Double Fire Zinnia (AAS-Winning Fully Double Brilliant Orange)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Zahara Double Fire, a 2010 All-America Selections winner, bears fully double, brilliant orange flowers on compact, disease-resistant plants, part of the heat-tolerant Zahara landscape zinnia series.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 10-14 inches. Zahara Double Fire, a 2010 All-America Selections winner, bears fully double, brilliant orange flowers, an unusual double form within the interspecific Zahara series that is best known for single blooms, on a compact, mounding, heat- and mildew-resistant plant well suited to landscape bedding. Like other Zahara selections it flowers continuously from spring through frost with minimal deadheading and tolerates humid Gulf South summers far better than traditional Zinnia elegans. Grow in full sun with good air circulation.

common_name: Zahara Starlight Rose Zinnia (AAS-Winning White Striped with Rose-Pink)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Zahara Starlight Rose, a 2010 All-America Selections winner, bears white single flowers striped with rose-pink, part of the heat-tolerant Zahara landscape zinnia series.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 10-14 inches. Zahara Starlight Rose, a 2010 All-America Selections winner, bears white single flowers irregularly striped and flecked with rose-pink, a distinctive bicolor pattern within the interspecific Zahara series on a compact, mounding, heat- and mildew-resistant plant well suited to landscape bedding. Like other Zahara selections it flowers continuously from spring through frost with minimal deadheading and tolerates humid Gulf South summers far better than traditional Zinnia elegans. Grow in full sun with good air circulation.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Exquisite bears extra-large double blooms ranging from magenta to soft rose on tall 2-4 foot plants.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 12-18 inches. Exquisite bears extra-large, fully double blooms ranging from rich magenta to soft dusty rose across the same planting, giving a naturally varied palette of related pink-purple tones on tall, vigorous stems reaching two to four feet, excellent for cutting. Plants bloom heavily from midsummer through the first frost with regular deadheading or harvesting to encourage continuous production. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.

common_name: Aztec Sunset Zinnia (Fleuroselect Gold Medal Double Bicolor Cream-Gold-Rust)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Aztec Sunset, a Fleuroselect Gold Medal winner, bears double bicolor blooms in cream, gold, rust, and red on dwarf bushy plants.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 8-12 inches. Aztec Sunset, a Fleuroselect Gold Medal winner in the Mexican zinnia species, bears small, double blooms blending cream, gold, rust, and red in a warm, autumnal color mix on a dwarf, densely branching, bushy plant, distinct from the larger single blooms of many Zinnia haageana selections. Its compact size and heavy, prolific flowering make it excellent for edging, containers, and mass plantings. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.

common_name: Old Mexico Zinnia (AAS-Winning Mahogany-Red Double Tipped Gold)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Old Mexico, a 1962 All-America Selections winner and RHS Award of Garden Merit holder, bears mahogany-red double and semi-double flowers tipped gold on a compact 12-18 inch mound.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 8-12 inches. Old Mexico, a 1962 All-America Selections winner holding a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit, bears rich mahogany-red, double and semi-double flowers with each petal tipped in gold, a warm, richly textured bicolor pattern on a compact, well-branched mound. Its dense, prolific flowering and manageable size have kept it a garden favorite for over sixty years. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.
